chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the man who recites the Sajdah verse at the end of the Surah.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should prostrate (Sajdah), then stand up and recite the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatihah), then bow (Ruku') and prostrate (Sajdah).'

key_terms.السَّجْدَة: Sajdah (prostration), specifically referring to the prostration due to reciting or hearing a specific verse of the Quran.
key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَاب: The Opening of the Book, referring to Surah Al-Fatihah, the first chapter of the Quran.
key_terms.يَرْكَع: He bows, referring to the Ruku' position in Islamic prayer.
key_terms.يَسْجُد: He prostrates, referring to the Sajdah position in Islamic prayer.

ai.seo_question: What is the correct procedure for Sajdah when reciting a Sajdah verse at the end of a Surah during prayer?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedural sequence for reciting prostration verses (Ayat al-Sujdah) within the obligatory prayer, specifically addressing the scenario where the verse appears at the end of a Surah. It establishes that the prostration is performed immediately upon recitation, followed by the recitation of Al-Fatihah to complete the current Rak'ah before moving to bowing (Ruku) and the second prostration. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the integrity of Al-Fatihah as a pillar of the prayer even when supplementary verses are recited.
